title: High Availability Patterns
description: Design multi-AZ architectures with auto scaling, load balancing, and failover for resilient applications.

data.text: **High availability (HA)** means your application stays operational even when individual components fail. On AWS, HA is achieved through redundancy across multiple Availability Zones (AZs) and automatic recovery.

An Availability Zone is an isolated location within an AWS Region. By deploying resources across multiple AZs, you protect against data center failures. AWS services like RDS, EBS, and ELB natively support multi-AZ deployments.

data.title: HA Components
items: **Application Load Balancer** — distributes traffic across targets in multiple AZs
**Auto Scaling** — replaces unhealthy instances and scales based on demand
**Health checks** — monitor instance health and remove unhealthy targets
**Multi-AZ RDS** — automatic failover to a standby in another AZ
**Route 53 health checks** — DNS failover to a secondary region

data.title: HA Tip
data.text: Always deploy your application across at least two Availability Zones. A single-AZ deployment is not fault-tolerant.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Multi-AZ deployments protect against data center failures
Load balancers distribute traffic and detect unhealthy targets
Auto Scaling replaces failed instances automatically
Database failover happens automatically with Multi-AZ RDS
